body.title: WIP: Add loadKeyCfgTransition / ARTIFACTSV4_SECRET* ARTIFACTSV4_KEYS_ACCEPTED
body.body:
Pursuing the goal of retiring the generalSigningSecret (previous changes toward that goal in #11194 #12307 #14385 and likely others), we add ini directives to configure the actions actifacts url signing secret using the now established generic signing and verification key methods:

```
[actions]
;; Signing keys for artifacts URLS.
;; _SECRET will be automatically added unless present
;; Algorithm is always HS256
;ARTIFACTSV4_SECRET =
;ARTIFACTSV4_SECRET_URI =
;ARTIFACTSV4_KEYS_ACCEPTED =
```

Unless `ARTIFACTSV4_SECRET` or `ARTIFACTSV4_SECRET_URI` are present, `ARTIFACTSV4_SECRET` will be automatically added as with other secrets, but it will be initialized with the generalSigningSecret to keep existing URLs valid.

The main improvements are that now the artifacts signing secret can be configured independently at all, and through `ARTIFACTSV4_KEYS_ACCEPTED` seamless key transitions as explained in https://forgejo.org/docs/next/admin/advanced/jwt-key-management-and-rotation/ become possible (I should probably add that the configuration directives are not only used for JWTs).

The transition method is implemented by `setting.loadKeyCfgTransition()`

Note that this requires forgejo to write the configuration, and if this fails, user intervention is required. The error message looks similar to:

```
  ...s/setting/setting.go:160:LoadCommonSettings() [F] Unable to load
  settings from config: save actions.ARTIFACTSV4_SECRET failed: failed
  to save "/etc/forgejo/app.ini": open /etc/forgejo/app.ini: permission denied
```

After enough of a transition phase (when the last release still using generalSigningSecret goes end of support), we can remove
loadKeyCfgTransition(), but until then, we need to touch the other places where GetGeneralTokenSigningSecret() is still used.

body.title: [v17.0/forgejo] fix: report errors to users when evaluating 'if' from actions
body.body:
**Backport:** https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14729

Fixes #14684.

When an error occurs evaluating `if: ...` on the server-side (a capability added in #13030), the implementation previously returned the error and interrupted the current workflow (inserting a job, emitting follow-up jobs, etc.).  This was not a great choice as it ends up with unexpected server-side errors, and the problem is not properly surfaced to the end-user who created the action.

This PR changes the behaviour so that those jobs are dispatched to runners, where `if` can be evaluated again.  The same error is expected to occur, but, that error will appear in the job logs and be reported to the user.

The downside to this change is that if server-side evaluation of `if` was ever 100% broken in some edge case -- where it *should* be able to be evaluated server-side, but instead was always sent to a runner -- that problem would be hidden as the jobs would be sent to runners and work successfully.  However, that outcome is OK; it's not performance optimal, but it's functional for users.

**Alternative:**  I considered reporting this error as a pre-execution error, instead.  There are two problems with this: fundamentally it turns into a run-ending error, rather than a job ending-error; and because of that, it's quite messy in the code as jobs would still need to be inserted into the database, *and* an error raised to a higher-level to mark the run as failed.  This simpler logic of dispatching the job to a runner seemed preferable to tackling these issues.

## Manual testing

Verified that all three conditions in #14684's table of expected conditions is accomplished.  The second row, "runs and then prints an error about the bad JSON", appears as this:

![image](/attachments/46c4fe38-507c-4dec-8f89-33aaf2be9b42)
